content:
claire (AE): starting a short thread for RetailPilot POC. customer asks: streaming SDK + tool/function call flow + enforce structured JSON output. also they want pricing impact and any enterprise blockers.

lucy_retail: hi! main constraints: EU data only, will need IP allowlist and short-lived creds. expected steady 150 qps, spikes to 900 qps during peak. can you confirm support for partner webhooks behind auth and how tool calls work?

diego (SE): yes — tool calls supported in streaming. typical flow: model emits a tool call event with a name and JSON args; client calls the tool and streams back the result. minimal example (node):

```js
// simplified pseudo-code
const c = new RedwoodClient(process.env.KEY)
const stream = c.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-2x', structured_output: true})
stream.send({role: 'user', content: 'Extract order_ids as JSON'})
for await (const ev of stream) {
  if (ev.type === 'tool_call') {
    // call internal webhook
    const result = await fetch('https://internal-hook.eu/api/enrich', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify(ev.args)})
    const body = await result.json()
    stream.sendToolResult(ev.tool, body)
  }
  if (ev.type === 'chunk') process.stdout.write(ev.chunk)
}
```

megan (DevEx): for structured output add a schema and `schema_enforce: strict`. runtime will reject mis-shaped outputs and surface a validation error you can catch. Example config flag: `schema_enforce: 'strict'`. This helps avoid silent regressions when models drift.

megan (DevEx): note on SDKs: Node/Go/Python all support streaming + toolcall. small gotcha — long-running toolcalls should stream partial progress back via incremental toolcall responses.

tariq (Security): checklist for POC access:
- EU data residency confirmation in order form
- IP allowlist (CIDR) for their ingress and partner webhook egress
- Short-lived credential pattern: we support temporary API keys via our token service or mTLS for Private deployments
- Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated/Private
- I'll need contact for their security person to complete our questionnaire

claire (AE): lucy can you share the webhook CIDRs and security contact? also are you open to an initial hosted trial then lift-and-shift to Dedicated?

lucy_retail: security contact is nina@retailpilot.com. webhooks run in eu-west and use these CIDRs: 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.128/25. fine with hosted trial then migrate.

diego (SE): capacity rec: for sustained 150 qps and 900 qps peaks, consider reserved pool with autoscale headroom. Ops snippet: 

```yaml
reserved:
  gpus: 3
  min_instances: 2
  max_instances: 10
  burst_buffer: true
```

megan (DevEx): pricing note: streaming doesn't change per-token unit price; billed tokens same as non-streaming. however streaming reduces latency and can lower overall request patterns (fewer retries), so effective cost may drop. I'll attach a short cost comparison after I run a quick sim.

ops-bot: Scheduled: deploy window 2024-12-02T08:00Z -> region eu-west-1. Monitor: p95 latency, toolcall-failure-rate.

claire (AE): action items:
1) tariq: send security questionnaire to nina (ETA: today EOD).
2) megan: run cost sim comparing hosted vs reserved for the qps profile and share spreadsheet (ETA: 48h).
3) diego: pack minimal sample apps (node/go/python) demonstrating streaming + toolcall + schema enforcement (ETA: 24h).
4) lucy: confirm webhook CIDRs in writing and whether webhook authenticates with mTLS or bearer tokens.

lucy_retail: will confirm auth method and loop in nina. pairing session at 15:00 CET tomorrow for integration walkthrough works for our infra team.

megan (DevEx): happy to pair. small tip: if you see toolcall timeouts, increase server-side tool timeout and ensure client reconnect logic tolerates partial failures.

claire (AE): thanks everyone — will keep notes here. we won't close until we have the security attestation and the sample apps validated. :white_check_mark:
